## Introduction: Probability and Statistics

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(kableExtra)
library(tidyverse)
```

- In this lecture we will review:
    - What is statistics?
    - What is probability?
    - What terminology do we use in probability and statistics?

## Introduction: Probability and Statistics

- What is (the practice of) statistics?
    - The science of collecting, organizing, summarizing, and analyzing information to draw conclusions or answer questions. 
    - This provides a measure of confidence in any conclusions.
    
- How do we measure confidence?
    - We use probability to quantify the likelihood of an event or outcome occurring. 
    - This allows us to make informed decisions based on data and uncertainty.

## Probability

- **Classical probability:** 

    - Suppose $N_e$ is the number of outcomes favorable to the event and $N$ is the total number of outcomes in the sample space. Then,

$$
P[\text{event}] = \frac{N_e}{N}
$$

- **Relative probability:**

    - Suppose an experiment is conducted $n$ different times, and the event occurs $n_e$ times. Then,
    
$$
P[\text{event}] = \frac{n_e}{n}
$$

## Unions 

- The **union** of two events $A$ and $B$, $A \cup B$, is the set of all outcomes that are included in *either* $A$ *or* $B$ (or both).

```{=html}
<svg viewBox="0 0 680 360" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     style="width: 88%; max-width: 880px; display: block; margin: 0 auto;
            font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif;">
  <!-- Event A circle (blue, shaded) -->
  <circle cx="226" cy="190" r="115"
          fill="#005EA6" fill-opacity="0.18"
          stroke="#005EA6" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <!-- Event B circle (green, shaded) -->
  <circle cx="398" cy="190" r="115"
          fill="#4A7B4F" fill-opacity="0.18"
          stroke="#4A7B4F" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <!-- Event A label -->
  <text x="226" y="138" text-anchor="middle"
        font-size="22" fill="#2c2b28" font-weight="700">Event A</text>
  <!-- Event B label -->
  <text x="398" y="138" text-anchor="middle"
        font-size="22" fill="#2c2b28" font-weight="700">Event B</text>
</svg>
```

## Intersection

- The **intersection** of two events $A$ and $B$, $A \cap B$, is the set of all outcomes that are included in both $A$ and $B$. 

```{=html}
<svg viewBox="0 0 680 360" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     style="width: 88%; max-width: 880px; display: block; margin: 0 auto;
            font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif;">
  <defs>
    <clipPath id="clipA">
      <circle cx="226" cy="190" r="115"/>
    </clipPath>
  </defs>
  <!-- Intersection shading only: circle B, clipped to circle A's boundary -->
  <circle cx="398" cy="190" r="115"
          fill="#3B6E64" fill-opacity="0.4"
          clip-path="url(#clipA)"/>
  <!-- Event A outline -->
  <circle cx="226" cy="190" r="115"
          fill="none" stroke="#005EA6" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <!-- Event B outline -->
  <circle cx="398" cy="190" r="115"
          fill="none" stroke="#4A7B4F" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <!-- Event A label -->
  <text x="226" y="138" text-anchor="middle"
        font-size="22" fill="#2c2b28" font-weight="700">Event A</text>
  <!-- Event B label -->
  <text x="398" y="138" text-anchor="middle"
        font-size="22" fill="#2c2b28" font-weight="700">Event B</text>
</svg>
```



## Mutually Exclusive

- Two events $A$ and $B$ are said to be **mutually exclusive** if the occurrence of one of the events excludes the possibility of the occurrence of the other event.

```{=html}
<svg viewBox="0 0 680 360" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     style="width: 88%; max-width: 880px; display: block; margin: 0 auto;
            font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif;">
  <!-- Event A circle (blue, solid) -->
  <circle cx="190" cy="190" r="115"
          fill="none" stroke="#005EA6" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <!-- Event B circle (green, solid) -->
  <circle cx="490" cy="190" r="115"
          fill="none" stroke="#4A7B4F" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <!-- Event A label -->
  <text x="190" y="138" text-anchor="middle"
        font-size="22" fill="#2c2b28" font-weight="700">Event A</text>
  <!-- Event B label -->
  <text x="490" y="138" text-anchor="middle"
        font-size="22" fill="#2c2b28" font-weight="700">Event B</text>
</svg>
```

## Complement

- The **complement** of an event $A$, $A^c$, is the event that $A$ *does not* occur.

```{=html}
<svg viewBox="0 0 680 360" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
     style="width: 88%; max-width: 880px; display: block; margin: 0 auto;
            font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif;">
  <!-- Complement shading: rectangle minus circle, via evenodd fill rule -->
  <path fill-rule="evenodd"
        d="M50,50 H630 V310 H50 Z
           M240,180 a100,100 0 1,0 200,0 a100,100 0 1,0 -200,0 Z"
        fill="#4A7B4F" fill-opacity="0.18"/>
  <!-- Sample space rectangle outline -->
  <rect x="50" y="50" width="580" height="260" rx="10"
        fill="none" stroke="#2c2b28" stroke-width="2"/>
  <!-- Event A circle outline -->
  <circle cx="340" cy="180" r="100"
          fill="none" stroke="#005EA6" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  <!-- Sample space label: A with superscript c -->
  <text x="72" y="76" text-anchor="start"
        font-size="22" font-family="'DM Sans', sans-serif"
        fill="#2c2b28" font-weight="700">A<tspan baseline-shift="super" font-size="15">c</tspan></text>
  <!-- Event A label -->
  <text x="340" y="188" text-anchor="middle"
        font-size="22" font-family="'DM Sans', sans-serif"
        fill="#2c2b28" font-weight="700">A</text>
</svg>
```
